newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk government wants debate on military demands.
newsitem.headline: Turk government wants debate on military demands.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led coalition plans to ask parliament to debate a military statement demanding a government crackdown on Islamist activism, newspapers said on Thursday.
"We want parliament to have a general debate so that everything can be discussed," the Hurriyet daily quoted junior coalition party leader Tansu Ciller as saying.
Political analysts said the move was part of an attempt by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to delay putting into force anti-Islamist measures demanded by the military.
Hurriyet said Ciller, also the deputy prime minister, had agreed with Erbakan to take the issue to parliament. Other papers carried similar stories.
However, MPs are not obliged to vote on the crackdown.
Erbakan calmed tension between the government and the military on Wednesday when he signed a statement from the National Security Council calling for a reversal of recent Islamist militancy.

Istanbul stocks opened 7.58 percent up on optimism the squabble was over. Ministers must now debate the council's demands but Erbakan's office said no cabinet meeting was planned for Thursday, the traditional day for weekly meetings.
"There was no meeting on the agenda anyway. Is is unclear when it will be," a prime ministry official told Reuters.
